correctness.rationale: Permutation averaging preserves the two factorial moments and the unanimity event, so the problem reduces exactly to a probability law for \(K=\sum_iX_i\) with \(EK=np\) and \(E[K(K-1)]=n(n-1)p^2\). On the outer branch the consecutive-root quadratic \((k-r)(k-r-1)/(r(r+1))\) majorizes the indicator of \(\{0,n\}\) on the integer support, and the displayed three-point law on \(\{0,r,r+1\}\) attains equality. For even \(n=2m\), the centered quadratic \((k-m)^2/m^2\) is the sharp majorant on the central interval and the law on \(\{0,m,n\}\) attains equality. The branch interval and all weights follow by the two moment equations. The inspected exact-rational verifier independently enumerates every three-support LP vertex in 693 bounded parameter cases and matches the symbolic formula; the proof itself is the integer quadratic majorant argument.

originality.rationale: The closest bounded-independence papers optimize the single endpoint that all bits equal one. Kwerel's classical aggregated-probability work gives sharp moment bounds for individual exact-count probabilities and other standard aggregates, but the accessible statement does not identify the simultaneous two-endpoint objective. Separate sharp bounds for \(K=0\) and \(K=n\) do not imply the maximum of their sum: on the even central branch the optimizer assigns positive mass to both endpoints and uses a different centered quadratic. Targeted Resultary search found no earlier theorem with this two-ended envelope or parity transition.
residual_risks: Older discrete moment-problem literature, especially Kwerel/Boros--Prékopa style aggregated-probability results, may contain the same two-endpoint LP under different terminology.

value.rationale: Unanimity is a canonical symmetric event under limited independence, and the theorem gives its complete sharp two-moment envelope, explicit extremizers, and an exact parity phase transition. It is a natural completion of the well-studied all-ones endpoint problem rather than an arbitrary finite slice.

final_claim: For \(n\ge2\), among Bernoulli vectors with common marginal \(p\) and pairwise independence, the sharp unanimity probability \(\Pr(X_1=\cdots=X_n)\) is the stated piecewise formula: an outer branch with \(r=\lceil(n-1)\min(p,1-p)\rceil\), and for even \(n\) a central quadratic branch; in particular the fair value is \(1/(n+1)\) for odd \(n\) and \(1/n\) for even \(n\).
limitations: Identical Bernoulli marginals and pairwise independence only.
The event is two-ended unanimity; no heterogeneous-marginal or higher-wise-independence formula is claimed.
